question_original: How can I protect myself from STIs and HIV?
question_english: How can I protect myself from STIs and HIV?
answer_local: Nea ɛbɛyɛ na woabɔ wo ho ban afi STI ne HIV ho no, ɛho hia sɛ wode kɔndɔm di dwuma yiye na ɛkɔ so daa. Afei nso, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ wo nhwehwɛmu mpɛn pii ansa na woatumi akɔ HIV mmoawa yi bi, na wɔhyɛ wo hokani no nkuran ma ɔno nso nyɛ saa ara. Wotwe wo ho firi nna mu anaa nna mu nneyɛeɛ a wobɛtwentwɛn so no nso bɛtumi ama asiane a ɛwɔ wo mu no so ate. Bio nso, sɛ wo ne obi a wɔasɔ no ahwɛ na onni STI ne HIV wɔ abusuabɔ a wodi nokware mu a, ebetumi aboa. Sɛ wowɔ nsɛmmisa bi a ɛha wo a, wobɛtumi akɔ Sheplus Ghana wɔ 055054 5672 anaa 0800 00 11 22 akɔhwehwɛ mmoa ne akwankyerɛ. Kae sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bɛkasa ama wɔn ankasa afotuo.
answer_english: To protect yourself from STIs and HIV, it's essential to practice safe sex by using condoms correctly and consistently. You should also get tested regularly for STIs and HIV, and encourage your partner to do the same. Abstaining from sex or delaying sexual activity can also reduce your risk. Additionally, being in a mutually faithful relationship with someone who has been tested and is free of STIs and HIV can help. If you have any concerns or questions, you can reach out to SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support and guidance. Remember to speak with a health worker for personal advice.

question_original: What changes happen to my body during puberty?
question_english: What changes happen to my body during puberty?
answer_local: Wɔ wo mmeranteberem no, wo nipadua no bɛfa nsakrae pii mu. Mmaayewa deɛ, nea ɛka wei ho ne nufoɔ a ɛtumi nyini, asensene a ɛtrɛ, ne brayɛ mfitiaseɛ. Wɔ mmarimaa fam no, nsakrae betumi ayɛ ɔbarima no barima anaa ɔbea no barima no nyin, ɛnne a emu dɔ, ne anim nhwi a ɛyɛ fɛ. Saa nsakraeɛ yi bɛtumi ayɛ sononko ama obiara na ɛkɔ so mmerɛ binom mu, ne saa nti sɛ wodwene wo nipadua ho a, ɛho hia sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bɛkasa. Kae sɛ, wei yɛ nsɛm a ɛfa nneɛma nyinaa ho, na ɛsɛ sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bi kasa ma w'ankasa w'adwennwene, wobɛtumi nso akɔ Sheplus Ghana wɔ 055 054 5672 anaa 06800 1122 mu ama wɔaboa wo.
answer_english: During puberty, your body will go through many changes. For girls, this may include breast growth, widening of hips, and the start of menstruation. For boys, changes may include growth of the penis and testicles, deepening of the voice, and appearance of facial hair. These changes can be different for everyone and happen at different times, so it's essential to speak to a health worker if you have concerns about your body. Remember, this is general information, and you should talk to a health worker for personal concerns, you can also reach out to SHEplus Ghana on 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support.

question_original: What is consent and how do I know if I am in a safe relationship?
question_english: What is consent and how do I know if I am in a safe relationship?
answer_local: Yɛlimaŋli gbinni nyɛla, kaman yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu la bee yurilim biɛhigu shɛli, niriba zaa ni mali suhuri pam. Di ŋmanila taba yɛlibu "ii". Di simdi ni a mali jilima, ka lan wum a suhupiɛlli, ka simdi ni a niŋ amaŋmaŋ’ gahinda. A yi bi baŋ, bɔhim’ amaŋa: n ni tooi yɛli ni dabiɛm bee n-lihiri? N suhuri mali suhupiɛlli ka zali saha ŋɔ? answer_english: Consent means agreeing to something, like a physical touch or a romantic relationship, where both people feel comfortable and willing. It's like saying "yes" together. In a safe relationship, you should feel respected, heard, and free to make your own choices. If you're unsure, ask yourself: can I say no without feeling scared or guilty? Do I feel happy and supported most of the time? Remember, you deserve to be treated with kindness and respect. question_english: What happens to my body during pregnancy?
answer_local: Nyinsɛn mu no, nsakrae pii bɛba wo nipadua no mu. Wo yafunu bɛyɛ kɛseɛ berɛ a abɔfra no renyini no, na ɛbɛtumi ama woate brɛ, ɔkɔm de wo, anaa wote nka sɛ woabrɛ. answer_english: During pregnancy, your body will go through many changes. Your belly will grow as the baby develops, and you may feel tired, hungry, or emotional. Your breasts may also become bigger and more sensitive. You may experience morning sickness, which is feeling nauseous or vomiting, especially in the first few months. Remember, this is general information, and if you have any personal concerns or questions, it's best to speak to a health worker for advice and support - you can also reach out to SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for guidance.

question_original: What are the signs of pregnancy and what should I do?

answer_local: If you think you might be pregnant, some common signs include missing your period, feeling tired, having morning sickness, or noticing changes in your breasts. question_original: How can I protect myself from STIs and HIV?
question_english: How can I protect myself from STIs and HIV?
answer_local: Nea ɛbɛyɛ na woabɔ wo ho ban afi STI ne HIV ho no, ɛho hia sɛ wode kɔndɔm di dwuma yiye na ɛkɔ so daa. Afei nso, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ wo nhwehwɛmu mpɛn pii ansa na woatumi akɔ HIV mmoawa yi bi, na wɔhyɛ wo hokani no nkuran ma ɔno nso nyɛ saa ara. Wotwe wo ho firi nna mu anaa nna mu nneyɛeɛ a wobɛtwentwɛn so no nso bɛtumi aboa ama asiane a ɛwɔ wo mu no so ate. Bio nso, sɛ wo ne obi a wɔasɔ no ahwɛ na ɔwɔ HIV no wɔ abusuabɔ a emu yɛ den mu a, ebetumi ama asiane a ɛwɔ hɔ no so atew. Wowɔ dadwene anaa nsɛmmisa bi a, kae sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bi bɛkasa, na wobɛtumi nso ne Sheplus Ghana adi nkitaho wɔ 055 054 5672 anaa 0800 00 1122 mu de agye mmoa ne akwankyerɛ.
answer_english: To protect yourself from STIs and HIV, it's essential to practice safe sex by using condoms correctly and consistently. You should also get tested regularly for STIs and HIV, and encourage your partner to do the same. Abstaining from sex or delaying sexual activity can also help reduce your risk. Additionally, being in a mutually faithful relationship with someone who has been tested and is HIV-negative can also lower your risk. If you have any concerns or questions, remember to speak with a health worker, and you can also contact SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support and guidance.

question_original: What changes happen to my body during puberty?
question_english: What changes happen to my body during puberty?
answer_local: Wɔ wo mmeranteberem no, wo nipadua no bɛfa nsakrae pii mu. Mmaayewa deɛ, nea ɛka wei ho ne nufoɔ a ɛtumi nyini, asensene a ɛtrɛ, ne brayɛ mfitiaseɛ. Wɔ mmarimaa fam no, nsakrae betumi ayɛ ɔbarima no barima anaa ɔbea no barima no nyin, ɛnne a emu dɔ, ne anim nhwi a ɛyɛ fɛ. Saa nsakraeɛ yi tumi si mmerɛ binom mu ma obiara, ɛno nti ɛyɛ adeɛ a ɛsɛ sɛ wohunu no sɛ ɛrekɔ so ntɛmntɛm sene wo nnamfonom. Wodwene wo nipadua ho a, ɛbɛyɛ papa sɛ wobɛkasa akyerɛ apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ ama w'ankasa afotuo, na wobɛtumi nso afrɛ Sherplus Ghana sɛ 055 054 5672 anaa 000 1122 de agye mmoa.
answer_english: During puberty, your body will go through many changes. For girls, this may include breast growth, widening of hips, and the start of menstruation. For boys, changes may include growth of the penis and testicles, deepening of the voice, and appearance of facial hair. These changes can happen at different times for everyone, so it's normal if you notice them happening at a different pace than your friends. If you have concerns about your body changes, it's best to speak to a health worker for personal advice, and you can also call SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support.

question_original: Is it normal to have irregular periods?
question_english: Is it normal to have irregular periods?
answer_local: Aane, mpɛn pii no, mmerɛ a ɛnkɔ so daa, ne titire ne berɛ a ɛdi kan a wofiri aseɛ twetwe adwene. Wo nipadua no gu so ara reyɛ nsakrae wɔ nipadua no mu, enti ebia wo mmere bɛyɛ nea wontumi nhu. Ebetumi agye mfe kakraa bi ansa na bere a wode yɛ adwuma no atu mpɔn. Sɛ mogya tu wo anaasɛ mogyaborosoɔ, mogya anaa mogyaborosoɔ tu wo a, ɛbɛyɛ papa sɛ wobɛkasa akyerɛ apɔmuden ho adwumayɛfoɔ ama w'ankasa afotuo. Wobɛtumi nso afrɛ Sheplus Ghana sɛ 055 054 5672 anaa 080 00 1122 ama mmoa ne akwankyerɛ wɔ brayɛ apɔmuden ho.
answer_english: Yes, it's common to have irregular periods, especially when you first start menstruating. Your body is still getting used to the hormonal changes, so your periods might be unpredictable. It can take a few years for your periods to become more regular. If you're worried about your periods or have heavy bleeding, pain, or other concerns, it's best to speak to a health worker for personal advice. You can also call SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support and guidance on menstrual health.

question_original: What contraception options are available for young people?
question_english: What contraception options are available for young people?
answer_local: Nneɛma pii wɔ hɔ a mmabunu betumi apaw de asiw nyinsɛn ano wɔ Ghana, a nea ɛka ho ne kɔndɔm, nnuru a wɔde siw awo ano, ne nneɛma a wɔde hyɛ nipadua no mu. Kɔndɔm yɛ ade pa a wobetumi apaw efisɛ wɔbɔ wɔn ho ban fi nyarewa a wonya fi nna mu (STI) nso ho. Ɛho hia sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bi kasa sɛ wobɛpɛ ɔkwan papa a wobɛfa so anya nsɛm a ɛyɛ nokware. Kae sɛ, nyinsɛn ano aduru yɛ ankorankoro gyinaesi, na ɛho hia sɛ wosi gyinae a nyansa wom. Wowɔ nsɛmmisa anaasɛ wohia akwankyerɛ a, wobɛtumi afrɛ SHEplus Ghana sɛ 055 054 5672 anaa 080 00 1122 ama wɔaboa wo.
answer_english: There are several contraception options available for young people in Ghana, including condoms, birth control pills, and injectables. Condoms are a good option because they also protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). It's essential to talk to a health worker to find the best option for you and to get accurate information. Remember, contraception is a personal choice, and it's crucial to make an informed decision. If you have questions or need guidance, you can call SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support.
